checks: The band widths are eventually disjoint and within the fixed affine neighborhoods. The chord gap on each intervening interval lies above H, with slopes separated from the adjacent slopes because the single H breakpoint stays a fixed positive distance from the two bands. The exterior slopes change in the convex direction.

On each band, symmetry and affinity give j∫_{band}H=r_i exactly. At the floor exp(−j²), the log factor is j²+O(1); the exp(−j²) correction to the reciprocal prefactor makes vanishing mass. Off the bands the distance-log integral is uniformly bounded by the finite number of gaps.

The reciprocal log excess is concentrated at t=0 and each band shrinks to the specified p_i. Its normalizer is 1/(M_jc_j)→2/c. The roof Jacobian gives the surface coefficient sqrt(2), and the side-face translation to v=t−δ_jH+η_j proves uniform near-edge log integrability.

All row data hold on the actual active H cells. Each defect band belongs to a fixed affine neighborhood, so its corresponding row limit is valid cellwise. The positive ordinary component makes the row barycenter interior; the limiting row value and volume weight are positive.

For a single atom of raw mass 2, the ordinary raw measure has mass 1 and first moments 1/2,1/4,1/4. Thus the atom changes only the first s moment to 1/2+2p_1 and the total mass to 3. This gives the displayed mark, limiting value c/6 and exact cap fraction 1/36.

The fixed-mark minimum follows from Jensen for log after original-volume reweighting and from concavity of the competing U under the tilted probability. It is a certificate at the fixed mark, with no requirement that that mark is deepest.
The original 9a1deed5372bf5ee §§6–7 has the same finite-band family, normalization, and exact contact certificate. The extra atomic mass lies at relative-interior positions as claimed.

overlap.comparison: The row/defect decomposition is compatible with this general contact theorem, which gives no actual arbitrary finite atomic realizability.

Its planar wedge realizes an atom at its exposed zero vertex with a scalar stress. It does not realize prescribed atoms in the relative interior of a tangential zero edge or the finite-family statement.

readability: The incidental comparison to the ordinary prism centroid follows from the standard centroid bound and does not enter the claimed defect or fixed-mark certificate.

summary: The shrinking affine bands realize every specified finite positive atomic tangential law, including the one-affine-row obstruction to tangential absolute continuity.
